arxiv-2107-06279.title: Dark Lepton Superfluid in Proto-Neutron Stars
arxiv-2107-06279.creator: Sanjay Reddy, Dake Zhou
arxiv-2107-06279.description: Abstract We find that sub-GeV neutrino portal bosons that carry lepton number can condense inside a proto-neutron star (newly born neutron star). These bosons are produced copiously and form a Bose-Einstein condensate for a range of as yet unconstrained coupling strengths to neutrinos.

arxiv-2204-05869.title: Assembly development for the Simons Observatory focal plane readout module
arxiv-2204-05869.creator: Erin Healy, Aamir M. Ali, Kam Arnold, Jason E. Austermann, James A. Beall, Sarah Marie Bruno, Steve K. Choi, Jake Connors, Nicholas F. Cothard, Bradley Dober, Shannon M. Duff, Nicholas Galitzki, Gene Hilton, Shuay-Pwu Patty Ho, Johannes Hubmayr, Bradley R. Johnson, Yaqiong Li, Michael J. Link, Tammy
arxiv-2204-05869.description: Abstract The Simons Observatory (SO) is a suite of instruments sensitive to temperature and polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) to be located at Cerro Toco in the Atacama Desert in Chile. Five telescopes, one large aperture telescope and four small aperture telescopes, will host roughly 70,000 highly multiplexed transition edge sensor (TES) detectors operated at 100 mK.

arxiv-2208-14522.title: Blow up in a periodic semilinear heat equation
arxiv-2208-14522.creator: Marco Fasondini, John King, J.A.C. Weideman
arxiv-2208-14522.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marco Fasondini, John King, J.A.C. Weideman. Blow up in a one-dimensional semilinear heat equation is studied using a combination of numerical and analytical tools. The focus is on problems periodic in the space variable and starting out from a nearly flat, positive initial condition. Novel results include various asymptotic approximations that are, in combination, valid over the entire space and time interval right up to and including the blow-up time. Preliminary results on continuing a numerical solution beyond the singularity are also presented.

arxiv-2304-01709.title: With great power (prices) comes great tail pipe emissions? A natural experiment of electricity prices and electric car adoption.
arxiv-2304-01709.creator: Johannes Mauritzen
arxiv-2304-01709.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Johannes Mauritzen. A fundemantal and unanswered question for the widely shared goal of electrifying passenger vehicles is how the price of electricity, which can vary greatly across countries and regions, affects buying behavior. I make use of a natural experiment in Norway in the period 2021-2022 when large price differences between north and south emerged to estimate the effect of electricity prices on the decision to purchase a pure battery-electric vehicle.

arxiv-2403-18996.title: Envisioning MedCLIP: A Deep Dive into Explainability for Medical Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2403-18996.description: Abstract Explaining Deep Learning models is becoming increasingly important in the face of daily emerging multimodal models, particularly in safety-critical domains like medical imaging. However, the lack of detailed investigations into the performance of explainability methods on these models is widening the gap between their development and safe deployment.

arxiv-2412-11885.title: Interpretable low-order representation of eigenmode deformation in parameterized dynamical systems
arxiv-2412-11885.creator: Nicolás Torres-Ulloa, Erick Kracht, Urban Fasel, Benjamin Herrmann
arxiv-2412-11885.description: Abstract Modal analysis has long been consolidated as a basic tool to interpret dynamics and build low-order models of mechanical, thermal, and fluid systems. Eigenmodes arising from the spectral decomposition of the underlying linearized dynamics represent spatial patterns in vibration, temperature, or velocity fields associated with simple time dynamics.

arxiv-2507-12007.title: Predictable Drifts in Collective Cultural Attention: Evidence from Nation-Level Library Takeout Data
arxiv-2507-12007.creator: Anders Weile Larsen, Vedran Sekara
arxiv-2507-12007.description: Abstract Predicting changes in consumer attention for cultural products, such as books, movies, and songs, is notoriously difficult. Past research on predicting the popularity of individual products suggests the existence of intrinsic prediction limits. However, little is known about the limits for predicting collective attention across cultural products.

pmc-10610669.title: Understanding Factors Contributing to Vaccine Hesitancy in a Large Metropolitan Area
pmc-10610669.creator: Paolo Montuori, Immanuela Gentile, Claudio Fiorilla, Michele Sorrentino, Benedetto Schiavone, Valerio Fattore, Fabio Coscetta, Alessandra Riccardi, Antonio Villani, Ugo Trama, Francesca Pennino, Maria Triassi, Antonio Nardone
pmc-10610669.description: Vaccine hesitancy has become a major global concern, leading to a significant decrease in the vaccination rate, with the World Health Organization recognizing it as one of the top ten threats to public health. Moreover, the health cost generated is evaluated to be 27 billion dollars per year in the US alone.

pmc-11494213.title: ﻿Description of two new species of the genus Trachelas L. Koch, 1872 and the male of T.gaoligongensis Jin, Yin & Zhang, 2017 from China (Araneae, Trachelidae)
pmc-11494213.creator: Gang Tang, Wen-long Yan, Yi Zhao, Xian-jin Peng
pmc-11494213.description: ﻿AbstractTwo new spider species of the genus Trachelas L. Koch, 1872 are described from China: Trachelaskavanaughisp. nov. (♀) and Trachelasventriosussp. nov. (♀). The male of Trachelasgaoligongensis Jin, Yin & Zhang, 2017 is described for the first time. Illustrations of the body and copulatory organs and a distribution map are provided.

pmc-11518777.title: Associations between maternal microbiome, metabolome and incidence of low-birth weight in Guatemalan participants from the Women First Trial
pmc-11518777.creator: Meghan L. Ruebel, Stephanie P. Gilley, Laxmi Yeruva, Minghua Tang, Daniel N. Frank, Ana Garcés, Lester Figueroa, Renny S. Lan, Hailemariam Abrha Assress, Jennifer F. Kemp, Jamie L. E. Westcott, K. Michael Hambidge, Kartik Shankar, Nancy F. Krebs
pmc-11518777.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundLow birth weight (LBW; <2,500 g) affects approximately 15 to 20 percent of global births annually and is associated with suboptimal child development. Recent studies suggest a link between the maternal gut microbiome and poor obstetric and perinatal outcomes. The goal of this study was to examine relationships between maternal microbial taxa, fecal metabolites, and maternal anthropometry on incidence of LBW in resource-limited settings.MethodsThis was a secondary analysis of the Women First trial conducted in a semi-rural region of Guatemala.

pmc-11652701.title: Clinical Outcomes of Pediatric Cancer Patients with COVID-19: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11652701.creator: Yasaman Arian, Pooya Faranoush, Fahime Ehsanipour, Negin Sadighnia, Ali Elahinia, Mohammad Faranoush
pmc-11652701.description: Background: Considering the widespread COVID-19 pandemic and its impact, especially on children, particularly those with cancer, in terms of transmission risk, mortality, and the occurrence of the disease based on various studies in different countries, we decided to conduct this study to improve the care of children with cancer regarding COVID-19.

pmc-11691739.title: UNDERSTANDING THE HOME-BASED SERVICE NEEDS FOR OLDER ADULTS: A SCOPING REVIEW FROM CHINA
pmc-11691739.creator: Hengyuan Zhang, Sifeng Zhang
pmc-11691739.description: The range of home-based services for older adults in China haven’t been clearly defined, which adversely affects their effectiveness in enhancing well-being. It is crucial to develop a better understanding of the home-based service needs of older adults. This paper employs a scoping review methodology to explore the service needs of older adults aging in place.

pmc-11884353.title: Steroid-induced Activated White Adipose Tissue on FDG PET-CT
pmc-11884353.creator: Ashique Rehman, Tejasvini Singhal, Parneet Singh, Girish Kumar Parida, Kanhaiyalal Agrawal, P. Sai Sradha Patro, T. Kishan Subudhi, Sunita Gupta
pmc-11884353.description: White adipose tissue (WAT) generally has negligible glucose utilization and thus, shows no or insignificant Fluorine-18 fluoro D-glucose (FDG) uptake. However, corticosteroids can cause altered biodistribution of FDG with increased uptake in WAT. We hereby describe a case of immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis showing diffusely increased FDG uptake in WAT secondary to high-dose corticosteroid therapy.

pmc-12508168.title: Aerodynamic dataset for selected doubly curved membrane canopy structures
pmc-12508168.creator: Anoop Kodakkal, Kimberly Adamek, Ann-Kathrin Goldbach, Tibebu Birhane, Rodrigo Castedo-Hernandez, Guillermo Martínez-López, Máté Péntek, Kai-Uwe Bletzinger, Roland Wüchner, Girma Bitsuamlak
pmc-12508168.description: A dataset of aerodynamic measurements is collected for doubly curved membrane structures as part of a comprehensive experimental testing campaign on wind effects on structural membranes conducted at the WindEEE Dome at Western University, Canada. Common doubly curved membrane geometries – the hypar, ridge valley, arch supported, cone, and umbrella – were tested in isolated instances.

pmc-12573984.title: Comparative genomic analysis of multiple mammary tumors from a single dog: whole-genome sequencing study
pmc-12573984.creator: Keon Kim, Tae-Hoon Shin, Sin-Wook Park, Sang-Ik Park, Yoon Jung Do, Woong-Bin Ro, Chang-Min Lee
pmc-12573984.description: BackgroundNext-generation sequencing of canine spontaneous cancer is a powerful approach in both comparative oncology and veterinary genomics. We encountered a unique case with concurrent mammary tumors. Using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), we profiled the tumor-specific landscape of somatic mutations across multiple tumor subtypes, providing unprecedented evidence within an identical genetic background.

pmc-12650076.title: From Lesion to Decision: AI for ARIA Detection and Predictive Imaging in Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-12650076.creator: Rafail C Christodoulou, Platon S Papageorgiou, Maria Daniela Sarquis, Ludwing Rivera, Celimar Morales Gonzalez, Daniel Eller, Gipsany Rivera, Vasileia Petrou, Georgios Vamvouras, Evros Vassiliou, Sokratis G Papageorgiou, Michalis F Georgiou, Masaru Tanaka, Simone Battaglia, Donato Liloia
pmc-12650076.description: Background: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains the leading cause of dementia worldwide, with anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies (MABs) marking a significant advance as the first disease-modifying therapies. Their use, however, is limited by amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), which appear as vasogenic edema or effusion (ARIA-E) and hemosiderin-related changes (ARIA-H) on MRI.

pmc-13167467.title: Suppression of PP2A-B56α drives EMT in EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-13167467.creator: Brittany N Heil, Garima Baral, Claire M Pfeffer, Mei B Bahler, Sanika S Gulavani, Emily G Smith, Lauren E Gartenhaus, Anna K Darling, Sydney J Clifford, Whitney Smith-Kinnaman, Kasi Hansen, Emma H Doud, Gaganpreet K Mall, Aaron N Hata, Nicole L Anderson, Matthew R Olson, Brittany L Allen-Petersen
pmc-13167467.description: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths in the United States, and ~50% of these patients present with metastatic disease at diagnosis. Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) is an important initiating step in the metastatic cascade that allows cells to acquire the migratory and invasive phenotypes necessary for dissemination.

pmc-13273470.title: Preliminary clinical and electrophysiological findings of NAc/ALIC deep brain stimulation strategy for treatment-resistant depression
pmc-13273470.creator: Wei Zhang, Botao Xiong, Yukun Kang, Yuan Gao, Ruiqing Yang, Qiang Wang, Wei Wang
pmc-13273470.description: SummaryEffective therapeutic options for treatment-resistant depression remain limited. This study investigated the clinical and electrophysiological effects of dual-target deep brain stimulation of the nucleus accumbens and anterior limb of the internal capsule. In a small patient cohort, the intervention was associated with reduced depressive symptoms and improved cognitive performance.

pmc-13292242.title: Iatrogenic ureteric catheterisation during routine community catheter change resulting in obstructive uropathy, urosepsis and multi-organ failure: a case report
pmc-13292242.creator: Jawwad Mihran Haider
pmc-13292242.description: Inadvertent ureteric catheterisation during urethral Foley catheter insertion is a rare iatrogenic complication, reported predominantly in females with neurogenic bladder. We describe an 80-year-old man with a long-term catheter for benign urethral stricture who presented with abdominal pain and acute kidney injury 24 hours after routine community catheter exchange.

pmc-13335611.title: Nutritional, Phytochemical, Mineral, and Morphological Variations in Hyacinth Bean (Lablab purpureus L.) Cultivars at Different Developmental Stages
pmc-13335611.creator: Gazi Wafa Akbar, Noshin Nower Bristy, Tania Ismail, Sabrina Mansur, Ahmed Saiyadeen Nusaha, Jobed Nahar, Rimon Barua, Afroze Anwar, Mubtasim Adnan, Nurul Absar
pmc-13335611.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The hyacinth bean ( Lablab purpureus L.), is a major winter legume in Bangladesh. However, there is very little information on how different cultivars and developmental stages of this legume affect its nutritional profile concerning pod composition. Consequently, the purpose of this study was to determine how both genotype and developmental stage (maturity) affect the morphological characteristics, proximate composition, phytochemical characteristics, and mineral composition of hyacinth bean pods grown in Bangladesh.

pmc-13475621.title: Whole-blood coagulation and platelet dynamics identify differential prothrombotic states in patients with rheumatoid arthritis treated with JAK or TNF-ɑ inhibitors
pmc-13475621.creator: Alessandro Giollo, Lorenzo Di Luozzo, Mariangela Salvato, Kiren Khalid, Riccardo D’Andrea, Andrea Benetti, Chiara Samà, Roberta Ramonda, Paolo Simioni, Luca Spiezia
pmc-13475621.description: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with inflammation-driven hypercoagulability and increased venous thromboembolic risk. Post hoc analyses of safety trials have raised concerns regarding a potential differential thrombotic risk with Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) compared with tumour necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi).
